claim_formal: For p uniform among primes ≤ x: ∀k, ∀ bounded continuous F:[0,1]^k→ℝ, lim_{x→∞} avg_{3≤p≤x} F(V_1(p),…,V_k(p)) = E F(L_1,…,L_k), (L_j) ~ PD(1), V_j = log q_j(p)/log(p−1)

quote_A.text: their logarithms, divided by log(p−1), converge in every finite joint distribution to the Poisson–Dirichlet distribution with parameter one

quote_B.text: This proves the conjecture of Ford, Konyagin and Luca.

notes: Limit-law identification coded M9 (asymptotic formula); M7 (limit = named law) is an alternative. Bundled: Erdős totient-fiber conjecture (∀ε ∃^∞ n: g(n)>n^{1−ε}), x^{1−o(1)} smooth shifted primes, and ∃^∞ p with μ(p−1)=1.

quote_A.text: \sum G(\pi) =\frac65c_*\frac{X^{5/6}}{\log X} +o\!\left(\frac{X^{5/6}}{\log X}\right)

quote_B.text: We prove Patterson's first-moment conjecture for normalized cubic Gauss sums over all primary Eisenstein primes, unconditionally.

notes: Previously known under GRH (Dunn–Radziwiłł); now unconditional. Lean also states angular-mode cancellation (secondary). Prefix could be read as ∀^∞ (o-asymptotic); chose none since it is one specific sequence.

claim_formal: ∀ alg. closed k, char p>3, ∀ projective lc threefold pair (X,B) with B effective ℚ-divisor, K_X+B ℚ-Cartier: (K_X+B nef ∧ ν(K_X+B)=1) → K_X+B semiample

quote_A.text: If (X,B) is a projective log canonical threefold pair with effective rational boundary, and K_X+B is ℚ-Cartier, nef, and of numerical dimension one, then K_X+B is semiample.

quote_B.text: We prove the numerical-dimension-one case of log abundance for threefolds over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 3.

notes: Abundance conjecture settled in one case (ν=1, dim 3, char>3); relies on Xu's nonvanishing and ν=2 results. Companion: terminal threefold version.

claim_formal: ∃ finitely generated normal integral ℂ-algebra A of dim 2, ∃ maximal ideal m: Der_ℂ(A) ≅ A^2 ∧ A_m not regular

quote_A.text: There exist a finitely generated normal integral \CC-algebra A of Krull dimension two and a maximal ideal \m\subset A such that Der_C(A) ≅ A^{⊕2}, A_m is not regular.

quote_B.text: This disproves the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero.

claim_formal: ∀ connected minimal compact complex surface X with b_1=1, b_2>0, κ=−∞: ∃ neighborhood U of S^3 in ℂ^2∖0, ∃ Σ⊂X open, ∃ biholomorphism U→Σ with X∖Σ connected

quote_A.text: every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with positive second Betti number contains a global spherical shell

quote_B.text: We prove the Global Spherical Shell conjecture

notes: Conjecture (Nakamura working hypothesis) is the positive-b2 case, so O1. Corollaries: topology/deformation type, Euler–signature inequality for aspherical surfaces.

quote_A.text: For every ε>0 there exists a finite constant C_ε such that ... ‖K_δ f‖_{L^3(S^2)} ≤ C_ε δ^{−ε} ‖f‖_{L^3(R^3)}.

quote_B.text: We prove the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions.

notes: Kakeya maximal conjecture is posed in all dimensions n; dimension 3 settled → O5 per rule 6 (O1 if the 3D case counts as its own problem). Builds on Wang–Zahl set theorem. Also bundled: 4D Hausdorff-dimension Kakeya conjecture (every Kakeya set in ℝ^4 has dim_H=4).

quote_A.text: There is a finite constant C such that ‖T(f_1,f_2,f_3)‖_{L^1} ≤ C ∏‖f_j‖_{L^3}

quote_B.text: resolving this case of the trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture

notes: Boundedness of a fixed operator at a single exponent triple; the full conjecture asks for a range of exponents.

claim_formal: ∃Λ ∀ infinite-dimensional real Banach space B ∃ compact K⊂B, Λ-doubling, ∀ finite-dim normed E: K admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into E

quote_A.text: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space.

quote_B.text: This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

notes: Lean CompactBanach matches the headline; Lean DoublingHilbert gives the ℓ2 version with explicit doubling constant 76800. Counterexample to a universal question → M3 (rule 5).

claim_formal: ∃C ∀k≥2 ∀ metric (X,d) with ≥k+1 points ∀s∈X^k ∃ randomized online policy A ∃B≥0 ∀ finite σ: E cost_A(σ) ≤ C log²(k+1)·OPT(σ) + B

quote_A.text: randomized k-server has competitive ratio O((log(k+1))^2) on every metric space against oblivious request sequences, matching the known worst-case lower bound

quote_B.text: It establishes the sharp squared-logarithmic order after the negative resolution of the original logarithmic conjecture.

notes: Claim itself is an upper bound (M8); coded M9 because the order is attained by the Bubeck–Coester–Rabani lower bound, so the worst-case order is determined. B as record → determined exactly (rule 7); P2/O1 also defensible. Companion: uniform polynomial-bit-cost implementation on rational metrics.

claim_formal: ∀q∈(0,1) ∀s∈(0,1] ∀c<1/(4 log 2) ∀^∞ n: T_{q,s}(n) ≥ n^{c log(q^3 log n)} (so n^{Ω(log log n)} traces needed)

quote_A.text: Exact worst-case reconstruction of a binary word from independent deletion traces requires n^{Ω(log log n)} samples for every fixed deletion probability

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the polynomial-sample question for binary trace reconstruction.

notes: Also bundled: uniform quasipolynomial-time decoder (upper bound) and polynomial bounds when deletion prob ≤ n^{−ε}. Lean also includes one-trace TV superpolynomial decay.

claim_formal: ∀ field K of char 0, ∀^∞ n, ∀ syntactically homogeneous ΣΠΣΠΣ circuit Φ over K computing IMM_{n,n}: size(Φ) ≥ n^{√n/400}; and ∀K ∀n≥2 ∃ such circuit of size ≤ n^{√n+4}

quote_A.text: Thus the gate complexity over characteristic-zero fields is n^{Θ(√n)}.

quote_B.text: The comparison addressed here is quantitative: we obtain the √n exponent in the balanced regime w=d=n for homogeneous five-layer circuits with unrestricted bottom linear forms.

notes: Sharp circuit-size order (M9); M10 (circuit complexity lower bound) is an alternative reading. No explicit posed problem: superpolynomial depth-5 bounds already followed from Limaye–Srinivasan–Tavenas; this determines the sharp exponent → coded P4/O1, but P5/O8 is plausible. Threshold n_0 not explicit (∀^∞), constant 1/400 explicit.

claim_formal: ∀ bounded strictly convex Ω⊂ℝ^2 with C^∞ boundary of positive curvature: (∃ T-invariant grazing annulus continuously foliated by individually invariant essential curves) → Ω is an ellipse

quote_A.text: Then Ω is an ellipse: there are c∈R^2 and a real symmetric positive-definite matrix Q such that Ω={x:(x−c)^TQ(x−c)<1}.

quote_B.text: This resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture in the stated smooth class.

notes: Rigidity statement coded M1 (integrable ⇒ ellipse); M5 if read as a characterization. The positively curved C^∞ class is the standard setting of the near-boundary conjecture, so O1; O5 if the conjecture is taken over a wider class. Companion: physical caustic-collar rigidity.

quote_A.text: Every set A⊆N with ∑ a^{−1}=∞ contains nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

quote_B.text: We prove Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

notes: Erdős Problem 4.33.6 (Erdős 1974; Erdős problems list) → P3. Matrix: existence of a progression inside A (M2); M1 reading ('A has property AP_k') is possible. Main quantitative theorem r_k(N) ≤ C_k N exp(−c_k (log N)^{ε_k}) is an M8 bound (ineffective-unspecified constants).

claim_formal: ∀ finite A={a_1..a_s}⊂ℝ^d, s≥2, affinely spanning: A is Ramsey ⇔ ∃P∈Mat_{d+1}(F⊗_ℚF) with (p_i⊗1)^T P (1⊗p_i)=0 ∀i and m_F(P_{αβ})=δ_{αβ}

quote_A.text: We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and sufficient tensor condition over their coordinate fields.

quote_B.text: some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader–Russell–Walters conjectured characterization

notes: Refutes the LRW conjecture and replaces it with a true criterion → O3. Consequences in Lean: all subtransitive sets Ramsey, ≤5 concyclic points Ramsey, generic 9-point circle configurations not Ramsey.

claim_formal: ∀ finite graph F ∃C_F ∃Δ_F ∀ F-free graph G with Δ(G)≥Δ_F: χ_DP(G) ≤ ⌈C_F Δ/log Δ⌉

quote_A.text: every F-free graph G of maximum degree Δ≥Δ_F satisfies χ_DP(G) ≤ ⌈C_F Δ/log Δ⌉

quote_B.text: This resolves the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov coloring conjecture in the stronger correspondence-coloring form.

notes: Lean CliqueFreeLog formalizes the companion AEKS independence result (α(G) ≥ c_r n log d/d for K_r-free G, Erdős Problem 802), not the coloring headline → different. Prefix could also be written ∀∃∀^∞∀ (degree threshold implicit).

claim_formal: ∃ finitely presented torsion-free group G (with finite 2-dim K(G,1)) ∃ α,β∈𝔽_2[G]∖{0}: αβ=0

quote_A.text: There exist a finitely presented torsion-free group G and nonzero elements α,β∈F_2[G] such that αβ=0.

quote_B.text: We disprove Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture

claim_formal: ∀ prime p, ∀ alg. closed k of char p, ∀ finite symmetric tensor category C over k: ∃n≥1 ∃ fiber functor C → Ver_{p^n}(k)

quote_A.text: there are an integer n≥1 and a fiber functor C ⟶ Ver_{p^n}(k)

quote_B.text: We prove the finite case of the Benson–Etingof–Ostrik conjecture

notes: Full BEO conjecture concerns moderate-growth categories; only the finite case is settled → O5. Corollaries: classification of incompressible finite categories (finite case of Coulembier–Etingof–Ostrik Conj. B).

claim_formal: ∀d≥3 ∀ iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor row law μ on ℤ^d ∀ℓ∈ℝ^d∖0: P_0(X_n·ℓ→+∞) ∈ {0,1}

quote_A.text: the probability of escape in each fixed nonzero real direction is zero or one

quote_B.text: We prove the directional zero–one conjecture for nearest-neighbor random walks in independent and identically distributed strictly elliptic environments on ℤd, d ≥ 3

notes: d=2 was known (Zerner–Merkl), so the full conjecture follows with prior results. Bundled: zero–one law for finite-range-dependent environments; ballisticity conjecture (Fribergh–Kious): directional transience ⇒ ballistic, iid uniformly elliptic, d≥2 (also Lean-formalized).

claim_formal: ∀ bounded smooth simply connected D with marked a,b, ∀ triangular-lattice approximations D_δ: uniform odd height h_δ with increments {0,±2} and ±1 two-arc boundary data satisfies h_δ ⇒ ḡ + σΦ_D in 𝒟'(D) as δ→0 (σ>0 universal)

quote_A.text: converges to a universal multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field

quote_B.text: This resolves the field part of Schramm's Problem 2.2.

notes: Family bundles three models; headline taken as the first one in the summary (Schramm Problem 2.2, field part only → O5 since the interface part is not settled). The real-valued model fully resolves Schramm Problem 2.3 (GFF + SLE4), which would be P3/O1; weighted integer model gives GFF for x∈[1/√2,1]. Scaling-limit identification coded M9; M7 is an alternative.

claim_formal: Con(ZF) → Con(ZF + PP + AC_wo + ¬AC)

quote_A.text: If ZF is consistent, then so is ZF+PP+AC_wo+¬AC.

quote_B.text: We prove that the Partition Principle does not imply the Axiom of Choice

notes: Answers the long-open 'does PP imply AC?' question: PP→AC is unprovable in ZF → O4 (independence); by rule 'O1/O2 follow wording' it could be O2. Not a named conjecture → P2. Lean PartitionConsistency matches; Lean PartitionPrinciple gives the transitive-model version.

claim_formal: ∀ group G ∀ 1≤m≤n ∀ w_1..w_m ∈ G*F_n: rank_ℚ(exponent-sum matrix)=m → ∃ overgroup H ⊇ G and h_1..h_n∈H with w_i(h)=1 ∀i (equivalently G → (G*F_n)/⟪w⟫ injective)

quote_A.text: Every finite nonsingular system of equations over an arbitrary group has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup.

quote_B.text: This proves Howie's conjecture on nonsingular systems.

notes: Theorem is stated as injectivity of the canonical map (∀, M1); headline phrasing is solvability (∀∃, M2). Lean Kervaire covers only the one-variable unimodular case (companion: Kervaire conjecture) → weaker.

claim_formal: ∀ even L ≥ 2304: E_1(L)−E_0(L) > log 20/784 for the spin-1 AF Heisenberg ring H_L (so liminf gap Δ_1 > 0)

quote_A.text: γ_L > \frac{\log20}{784} for every even L≥2304. Consequently Δ_1 ≥ \frac{\log20}{784} > 0.

quote_B.text: establishing the positive even-periodic formulation of the spin-one Haldane conjecture

notes: Explicit threshold → ∀ + effective (rule 2). Haldane's conjecture is about integer spins generally; spin one is the standard formulation, settled for even periodic rings → O1 (O5 if the general integer-spin conjecture is the posed problem). Companion: odd open chain with boundary field h=3/5, Tasaki index −1.

claim_formal: ∀ simple unitary strongly rational VOA V over ℂ: V is energy-bounded and CKLW-strongly local, A_V is a completely rational conformal net, V is completely unitary, and Rep(V) ≃ Rep^f(A_V) as braided unitary tensor categories

quote_A.text: Every simple unitary strongly rational vertex operator algebra generates a completely rational conformal net.

quote_B.text: Proves the strongly rational case of the strong-locality conjecture

notes: Matrix primary M1 (strong locality / complete rationality); the tensor-equivalence part is M7. Lean main covers only energy bounds, CKLW strong locality and an irreducible net (not complete rationality or the equivalence) → weaker.

claim_formal: ∃ separable unital C*-algebra A (=C*(ℤ[1/2]^3⋊(SL_3(ℤ)×ℤ))) ∀ nonzero unital nuclear B ∀ free ultrafilter ω: ¬∃ unital embedding A → B^ω

quote_A.text: For every nonzero unital nuclear C*-algebra B and every free ultrafilter ω on N, there is no unital embedding A→B^ω.

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem.

notes: Explicit witness still prefix ∃ (rule 1). Kirchberg's problem is a question, not a conjecture with predicted answer → P2.

claim_formal: ∀n≥1 ∀ locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group G ∀ faithful jointly continuous action of G on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological n-manifold without boundary: G is a Lie group

quote_A.text: A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological n-manifold without boundary is a Lie group.

quote_B.text: We prove the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension

notes: Main technical theorem: no faithful ℤ_p action on such manifolds (M4), with the classical reduction to the group statement. Second-countability/no-boundary hypotheses are standard.

claim_formal: im(⊕_{d>0} h_d: π_d^S → H_d(Q_0S^0;𝔽_2)) = span_𝔽2{h(η), h(ν), h(σ), h(θ_j) : θ_j exists}

quote_A.text: The image of ⊕_{d>0}h_d is spanned over F_2 by the Hurewicz images of the Hopf-invariant-one classes η,ν,σ ... and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes θ_j

quote_B.text: We prove Curtis's conjecture

notes: Exact determination of a specific image coded M9 (exact value); M7 (equality of two named subspaces) or M6 (complete list of spherical classes) are alternatives. Corollaries: Eccles's conjecture for spheres; image finite and vanishing above degree 126.

claim_formal: ∀ real reflexive Banach X ∀ nonempty closed bounded convex C⊆X ∀ nonexpansive F:C→C ∃x∈C: F(x)=x

quote_A.text: Every nonexpansive selfmap of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point.

quote_B.text: This resolves the reflexive-space fixed point problem for the given norm.

notes: Kirk's problem posed as a question (P2); P1 if read as a conjecture. Corollary: common fixed points of commuting families form a nonexpansive retract.

claim_formal: ∃ even N ∃ closed exact embedded Lagrangian L ⊂ T*(S^9×S^{N−1}): L ≅ S^9×S^{N−1} ∧ L not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section

quote_A.text: the manifold Q=S^9×S^{N−1} admits a closed exact smoothly embedded Lagrangian L⊂T^*Q such that L is diffeomorphic to Q and no compactly supported Hamiltonian isotopy carries the zero section to L

quote_B.text: We disprove the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture.

notes: N is only 'sufficiently large', not explicit.

claim_formal: ∃ smooth U(10)-invariant Kähler form ω_0 ∈ [ω_FS] on ℂP^10: maximal Calabi flow exists only on [0,T_*) with T_*<∞, and S(ω(t))(p) ~ a(T_*−t)^{−1/2}

quote_A.text: There is a smooth U(10)-invariant Kähler form ω_0 on CP^{10}, in the class [ω_FS], whose maximal smooth Calabi flow has existence interval [0,T_*) with 0<T_*<∞.

quote_B.text: This disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture, even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.

notes: Corollary: singularities in every complex dimension ≥10 via products.

claim_formal: ∀ stable finite-range radial potential Φ, ∀ C^1 initial density f_0 with Gaussian Bol-bounds, ∀ T such that the Boltzmann solution f exists with Gaussian bound on [0,T], ∀s≥1: lim_{ε→0} sup_{t≤T} ‖F^ε_s(t) − f(t)^{⊗s}‖_{L^1} = 0

quote_A.text: All fixed-order rescaled factorial marginals converge in L1, uniformly throughout every finite interval on which the classical kinetic solution has a uniform Gaussian bound.

quote_B.text: Deng, Hani and Ma extended the hard-sphere kinetic derivation through each prescribed interval on which the regular Boltzmann solution exists with the required bounds

notes: Hypothesis that a regular Boltzmann solution with Gaussian bound exists on [0,T] is part of the statement, not an unproved conjecture, so no conditional_on flag. Extends Deng–Hani–Ma (hard spheres, full lifespan) and Pulvirenti–Saffirio–Simonella (potentials, short time) → O8; P2 (long-time Boltzmann–Grad for potentials as an open problem) is also plausible. Limit identification coded M9 (M1/M7 alternative). Companion: hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations (fluctuating Boltzmann equation).

claim_formal: ∃ algorithm (M,w) ↦ effective smooth force f_{M,w} on flat 𝕋^3 such that ∀ M ∀ w, ∀ν>0: the zero-data forced Navier–Stokes solution exists, is unique and smooth, and the fixed particle a_* enters the fixed open strip O ⇔ M halts on w

quote_A.text: There is an algorithm taking a deterministic single-tape machine M and a finite word w to an effective smooth mean-zero force f_{M,w} ... The particle initially at a_* enters O at a finite time if and only if M halts on w.

quote_B.text: Here the flat torus and viscosity are fixed in advance and the fluid starts at rest. The machine and input instead enter an external force prescription.

notes: Universality / undecidability of particle reachability → M10. No explicitly posed problem cited; extends Euler/NS universality constructions (Cardona–Miranda–Peralta-Salas–Presas, Dyhr et al.) to forced viscous flows on the flat torus → P5/O8 (could be 'other': a new kind of result). Many variant manuscripts (eventually stationary, periodic, vanishing forcing, velocity detection).
